perspective:
From Carolyn Abebe’s perspective, she has access to the following information:

- Carolyn works as a bank teller at a community bank and has recently started working with Marilyn Olson as a colleague.
- During a busy week with increased customer traffic and stress, Carolyn observed Marilyn being unusually quiet and withdrawn, unlike Marilyn’s normally engaging demeanor.
- Carolyn asked Marilyn if everything was alright and whether she wanted to talk. Marilyn told Carolyn she was overwhelmed with work and some personal stuff, and thanked Carolyn for asking.
- In a later interaction, Carolyn experienced Marilyn responding curtly. Carolyn felt confused and slightly hurt by this.
- Carolyn then told Marilyn she hoped she hadn’t overstepped, that she had had tough times too, and that talking can sometimes help. Marilyn said she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- After that, Carolyn perceived Marilyn as responding positively. Carolyn felt relieved and hopeful about their friendship and invited Marilyn to a small weekend get-together. Marilyn said it sounded lovely, thanked Carolyn, and accepted.
- Despite friendly interactions outside work, Carolyn felt Marilyn was still maintaining a professional distance at the bank. Carolyn felt disappointed.
- Carolyn asked to talk about their work dynamic, saying she felt an unexplained distance between them. Marilyn said she hadn’t realized it, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving collaboration.
- After their private meeting, Carolyn believed they had cleared the air and understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. She felt content and optimistic.
- Carolyn proposed teaming up with Marilyn on the new project proposal. Marilyn said that was a great idea, was glad they had talked, and looked forward to working more closely with Carolyn.
